It is truly heartwarming to observe how high school dramas have convinced us that adolescence is merely a prelude to a Broadway musical, where the crushing weight of academic pressure and social anxiety can be effortlessly resolved by a well-timed tap routine. Why bother with the tedious, unglamorous work of actual communication or emotional maturity when you can simply out-dance your trauma? It is a marvel of modern storytelling that complex human struggles are so neatly packaged into synchronized choreography, proving that if you just move your feet fast enough, nobody will notice you have no idea what you are doing.

As for the primary material of a candle, it is, of course, wax. Specifically, the paraffin byproduct of petroleum refining, molded into a cylindrical shape to provide a warm, flickering glow that reminds us of our own fragility while slowly consuming the very air we breathe.
